title: How to reset a tripped GFCI outlet
summary: Reset once after unplugging loads; stop if the outlet will not hold.

blocks.heading: Dry hands, dry outlet, then reset
items: If the outlet is wet, hot, damaged, or smells burned, stop using it and have it checked.
With dry hands, unplug connected appliances and press RESET firmly.
If it resets, use TEST and RESET as the device instructions describe. If it trips again or won’t reset, leave it off and contact an electrician; do not keep forcing it.

items.label: Leviton: GFCI reset and lockout
items.detail: No incoming power, a continuing fault, or a failed device can prevent reset. This page does not cover wiring repairs.
